def rescale_clamped_pct(x, lo, hi):
    """Every evening, a fitness dashboard turns a raw sensor reading into a
    progress percentage for its display bar. The sensor sometimes reports
    values outside the calibrated range, so the reading has to be pulled
    back inside before the percentage is computed. lo and hi are ints with
    lo strictly less than hi; x is an int. First clamp x into [lo, hi]
    (values below lo become lo, above hi become hi). Then return the
    percentage position of the clamped x inside [lo, hi] as
    ((clamped_x - lo) * 100) // (hi - lo), using integer floor division
    exactly as written. The display bar only shows whole numbers, so this
    integer result is exactly what the front end expects.

    >>> rescale_clamped_pct(5, 0, 10)
    50
    >>> rescale_clamped_pct(-3, 0, 10)
    0
    """
